expectation: Membrane rings on T cells. These are common in tumour tissue: dense in lymphoid aggregates and stroma, with single cells scattered among tumour nests. Tumour epithelium should be mostly negative. CD3 should overlap with CD4 and pick up CD4-negative T cells too.
observed: A: discrete yellow cells, dense aggregates in some ROIs and sparse in others, not following nuclear density. B/C: a few scattered positive cells, nest areas negative. D: ring-like membrane staining around nuclei. E: CD3 sits on CD4 cells (white), plus CD3-only green.
why: T-cell-like membrane staining in aggregates and stroma, independent of nuclear density, that overlaps CD4 as expected.
notes: CD3 marks discrete cells, packed into aggregates in several ROIs and sparse in tumour nests. Most of its signal overlaps CD4 (white in the merge), with a CD3+CD4- subset that is likely CD8 cells. This is a clear, specific T-cell stain.
